Given (Context): Given the Planner is authenticated and the equipment unit is registered with full identification.
Then (Result): Then the system confirms the plan creation and displays it as scheduled in the operational calendar.
When (Action): When they select the equipment unit, define the calendar time frequency, and save the plan.

Given (Context): Given the Planner is authenticated.
Then (Result): Then the system reports the missing mandatory fields and does not generate the schedule.
When (Action): When they attempt to save a plan without selecting an equipment unit or without defining the frequency.

Given (Context): Given a recurring preventive plan has been successfully created.
Then (Result): Then they view the complete record with author, date and time, affected equipment unit, frequency, and configured method.
When (Action): When the user accesses the system's audit history.

Given (Context): Given there are active preventive plans.
Then (Result): Then the system presents the equipment unit, the maintainable item, the time frequency, the date of the next work order, and the status.
When (Action): When the Planner queries the list of plans.

Given (Context): Given the Technician has completed the physical work and the Work Order is in 'In Progress' status.
Then (Result): Then the system updates the Work Order status to 'Pending Review' and logs the technical reliability data.
User Story: Digital WO Closure with ISO 14224 Taxonomy (https://app.notion.com/p/Digital-WO-Closure-with-ISO-14224-Taxonomy-39287c56a82880fc8cecd71f40e671d1?pvs=21)
When (Action): When they fill out the closure form specifying the Maintainable Item, Failure Mode, Mechanism, and Cause according to ISO 14224, and submit the closure.

Given (Context): Given the Technician is filling out the WO closure form.
Then (Result): Then the system associates the image with the closure record and makes it visible for future technical audits.
User Story: Digital WO Closure with ISO 14224 Taxonomy (https://app.notion.com/p/Digital-WO-Closure-with-ISO-14224-Taxonomy-39287c56a82880fc8cecd71f40e671d1?pvs=21)
When (Action): When they capture or attach a photograph of the repaired equipment unit.

Given (Context): Given the Technician attempts to close a corrective Work Order.
Then (Result): Then the system blocks the closure, alerts about the missing technical data, and prevents the state transition.
User Story: Digital WO Closure with ISO 14224 Taxonomy (https://app.notion.com/p/Digital-WO-Closure-with-ISO-14224-Taxonomy-39287c56a82880fc8cecd71f40e671d1?pvs=21)
When (Action): When they omit the Failure Cause or any mandatory ISO 14224 taxonomic field.

Given (Context): Given the Technician is in a plant area without network coverage.
Then (Result): Then the system saves the record locally and automatically synchronizes it with the server once connectivity is restored.
User Story: Digital WO Closure with ISO 14224 Taxonomy (https://app.notion.com/p/Digital-WO-Closure-with-ISO-14224-Taxonomy-39287c56a82880fc8cecd71f40e671d1?pvs=21)
When (Action): When they register the WO closure with ISO 14224 classification.

Given (Context): Given the Technician is classifying a failure.
Then (Result): Then the system dynamically filters the available Failure Modes to show only those applicable to that specific item class.
User Story: Digital WO Closure with ISO 14224 Taxonomy (https://app.notion.com/p/Digital-WO-Closure-with-ISO-14224-Taxonomy-39287c56a82880fc8cecd71f40e671d1?pvs=21)
When (Action): When they select the Maintainable Item.

Given (Context): Given the Contractor is authenticated and assigned to the Work Order.
Then (Result): Then the system attaches the document, records the timestamp, and notifies the Supervisor.
When (Action): When they upload a PDF report and select the corresponding Maintainable Item.

Given (Context): Given the Contractor is attaching a report.
Then (Result): Then the system rejects the file, displays an invalid format error, and prevents the upload.
When (Action): When they attempt to upload a file with an unauthorized extension (e.g., .exe or .zip).

Given (Context): Given the Contractor is attaching a report.
Then (Result): Then the system rejects the file and displays an error indicating the maximum allowed size has been exceeded.
When (Action): When they attempt to upload a PDF file exceeding 50 MB.

Given (Context): Given a Contractor has uploaded a report.
Then (Result): Then they can view, download, and approve/reject the attached document directly from the interface.
When (Action): When the Supervisor reviews the Work Order details.

Given (Context): Given a digital report is attached to the Work Order.
Then (Result): Then the system analyzes the document and pre-fills the real hours, materials, and description fields with a high confidence indicator.
When (Action): When the Supervisor triggers the automatic extraction.

Given (Context): Given the attached report lacks material details.
Then (Result): Then it pre-fills the hours and description, flags the materials field as empty, and requires manual input from the Supervisor.
When (Action): When the system performs the automatic extraction.

Given (Context): Given the extraction returned data with high confidence.
Then (Result): Then the data is permanently saved to the Work Order record.
When (Action): When the Supervisor reviews the pre-filled fields and clicks 'Approve Extraction'.

Given (Context): Given a preventive plan is set to trigger every 500 operating hours.
Then (Result): Then the system automatically generates the Work Order and resets the cycle counter.
When (Action): When the equipment unit's telemetry counter crosses the 500-hour threshold.

Given (Context): Given a preventive Work Order triggered by usage has been closed.
Then (Result): Then the system records the reset of the cycle counter and logs the zero-point for the next iteration.
When (Action): When the Technician confirms the replacement of the component.

Given (Context): Given an Equipment Unit has a Criticality index of 8.
Then (Result): Then the system automatically assigns a RIME priority score of 40 to the task.
When (Action): When a Work Request is created with a Work Class index of 5.

Given (Context): Given the programming staff queries the pending tasks board.
Then (Result): Then the interventions with the highest RIME Score (scale 1 to 100) automatically appear at the top section of the backlog.
When (Action): When the system loads the list of work orders.

Given (Context): Given the Technician is performing a technical intervention and opens the intelligence assistant interface.
Then (Result): Then the engine responds with the retrieved technical information and provides the exact reference (document, page, and section) for manual validation.
When (Action): When they ask about a specific technical specification contained in the equipment manuals.

Given (Context): Given the Technician requests information unrelated to the available technical knowledge base.
Then (Result): Then the assistant communicates that it does not have reliable information in current manuals and suggests consulting the supervisor or reviewing physical documentation.
When (Action): When they perform a general or out-of-domain query.

Given (Context): Given the operational staff is in an area without network connectivity.
Then (Result): Then the system informs that the assistant is unavailable offline and presents the local search interface to query downloaded manuals.
When (Action): When they attempt to use the intelligence assistant.

Given (Context): Given a query to the intelligence assistant was made during an intervention.
Then (Result): Then they view the query log including the timestamp, technical question, and document sources referenced by the engine.
When (Action): When the supervisor reviews the work order history.

Given (Context): Given the Reliability Engineer is configuring the technical parameters of a Level 6 equipment unit.
Then (Result): Then the system confirms the successful boundary registration and the selected components are officially integrated into the equipment's technical record.
When (Action): When they record the physical boundary points and select the Level 8 components belonging to the equipment.

Given (Context): Given a technical component is already assigned to the boundaries of an operational equipment unit.
Then (Result): Then the system issues a hierarchical conflict notification and blocks the operation to prevent inconsistencies in the equipment database.
When (Action): When the technical staff attempts to link that same component to a different equipment unit in the hierarchy.

Given (Context): Given a user queries the technical record of an equipment unit in the operational app.
Then (Result): Then they view the technical description of the physical boundaries and the complete list of components that make up the operational unit.
When (Action): When they access the boundaries and included components section.

Given (Context): Given an operational equipment unit has valid warranty coverage according to system records.
Then (Result): Then the system interrupts the operational flow with a warning notification, informing about the active warranty and suggesting initiating a claim.
When (Action): When the technical staff attempts to initiate the registration of a corrective intervention for that equipment.

Given (Context): Given an active warranty notification was issued during work order management.
Then (Result): Then the system adapts the operational interface, hiding internal cost fields and presenting the manufacturer's contact info and coverage terms.
When (Action): When the responsible user chooses to formalize a technical claim with the provider.

Given (Context): Given an active warranty notification was issued.
Then (Result): Then the system demands the entry of a mandatory technical justification before allowing the formalization of the work order.
When (Action): When the responsible user decides to proceed with internal maintenance despite the active coverage.

Given (Context): Given the Project Engineer is on the new equipment unit registration interface.
Then (Result): Then the system formalizes the equipment unit registration, communicates the operation's success, and presents the newly created equipment's technical record.
When (Action): When they fill out the mandatory technical fields (identification, class, manufacturer, and operational dates) and request to save.

Given (Context): Given the industrial identifier (Tag) is already assigned to an existing equipment unit in the system.
Then (Result): Then the system issues a warning notification indicating the identifier is already in use and suggests reviewing the existing record.
When (Action): When the technical staff attempts to register a new equipment unit using the same identifier.

Given (Context): Given the creation of a new operational equipment unit is underway.
Then (Result): Then the system restricts the save action, highlights missing fields, and notifies about the failure to comply with ISO 14224 information requirements.
When (Action): When the user attempts to finalize the registration omitting mandatory technical classification (e.g. Equipment Class).

Given (Context): Given the technical staff enters the equipment's operational chronology.
Then (Result): Then the system detects the temporal inconsistency and communicates an integrity warning to ensure historical data accuracy.
When (Action): When an operation start date is registered that is prior to the equipment's acquisition or purchase date.

Given (Context): Given a critical spare parts order has been received at the storage facilities.
Then (Result): Then the system increases the physical inventory levels, records the chronological transaction, and communicates the successful receipt confirmation.
When (Action): When the responsible staff formalizes the inbound by specifying the spare part, quantity received, and technical location in the warehouse.

Given (Context): Given the Warehouse Manager processes a receipt for an order with discrepancies in the reference unit price.
Then (Result): Then the system records the physical inventory entry but generates an administrative alert for cost evaluation.
When (Action): When they complete the material receipt transaction.

Given (Context): Given two distinct functional storage locations are established.
Then (Result): Then the system updates the inventory levels simultaneously in both locations, maintaining global balance integrity.
When (Action): When the Warehouse Manager executes a stock transfer between locations.

Given (Context): Given an equipment unit is in the 'Onboarding' phase.
Then (Result): Then the system blocks the activation and demands the required documentation to ensure ISO 14224 compliance.
When (Action): When the Project Engineer attempts to activate the equipment without attaching the manufacturer's manual.

Given (Context): Given the Project Engineer approves an equipment unit.
Then (Result): Then the system records the author, timestamp, and review status in the equipment's permanent audit log.
When (Action): When the status transition is completed.

Given (Context): Given an equipment unit is pending validation.
Then (Result): Then the system rejects the approval, highlighting that physical boundaries are a mandatory prerequisite.
User Story: New Equipment Unit Validation and Onboarding (https://app.notion.com/p/New-Equipment-Unit-Validation-and-Onboarding-39287c56a8288002a1e2fe57718cda8d?pvs=21)
When (Action): When the Project Engineer attempts to approve it with undefined functional boundaries.

Given (Context): Given the stock level for a Class A spare part drops below the Reorder Point.
Then (Result): Then an automated alert is triggered to the purchasing department for immediate replenishment.
User Story: New Equipment Unit Validation and Onboarding (https://app.notion.com/p/New-Equipment-Unit-Validation-and-Onboarding-39287c56a8288002a1e2fe57718cda8d?pvs=21)
When (Action): When the transaction is processed by the system.

Given (Context): Given the stock level for a spare part exceeds the defined Maximum Stock limit.
Then (Result): Then the system logs the transaction but flags the event as an overstock anomaly.
When (Action): When a material receipt is recorded.

Given (Context): Given the Warehouse Manager accesses the replenishment monitor.
Then (Result): Then the system exclusively displays high-impact items that are near or below their safety stock threshold.
When (Action): When they filter by 'Class A' criticality.

Given (Context): Given an upcoming scheduled Work Order reserves a specific spare part quantity.
Then (Result): Then it issues a pre-emptive alert if the projected stock falls below the Reorder Point before the intervention date.
When (Action): When the system calculates the projected available stock.

Given (Context): Given a failed equipment unit needs replacement at a specific Functional Location.
Then (Result): Then the system records the equipment transition, preserves the Functional Location's reliability history, and updates the physical location of both units.
When (Action): When the Planner unlinks the current equipment unit and links an identical available equipment unit from the warehouse.

Given (Context): Given a Planner attempts an equipment swap.
Then (Result): Then the system blocks the swap, warning about a classification mismatch.
When (Action): When they try to link an equipment unit of a different Technical Class to the Functional Location.

Given (Context): Given a successful equipment swap has been executed.
Then (Result): Then the removed equipment unit is automatically assigned a 'Workshop' or 'Pending Repair' status.
When (Action): When the system finalizes the transaction.

Given (Context): Given an equipment swap is performed.
Then (Result): Then they see the exact timestamps and locations for both the unlinked and newly linked equipment units.
When (Action): When the Auditor reviews the equipment's history.

Given (Context): Given the Administrator is setting up the plant's operational structure.
Then (Result): Then the system creates the location, making it available for equipment unit assignment.
When (Action): When they create a Functional Location ensuring it has a unique alphanumeric ID and an assigned superior hierarchy level.

Given (Context): Given a Functional Location with the ID 'ZON-01' already exists.
Then (Result): Then the system blocks the creation and displays a uniqueness error.
When (Action): When the Administrator attempts to create a new location with the exact same ID.

Given (Context): Given the Administrator is configuring a Functional Location.
Then (Result): Then the system requires the parent assignment to comply with the ISO 14224 hierarchical structure.
When (Action): When they attempt to save it without assigning a parent location (except for the root Plant level).

Given (Context): Given the Warehouse Manager registers a new spare part.
Then (Result): Then the system generates the Part Master record, standardizing the material across the plant.
When (Action): When they input the Commodity Code, description, manufacturer, and ABC class.

Given (Context): Given the responsible staff classifies a material for direct acquisition (no storage).
Then (Result): Then the system adapts the technical interface, hiding storage parameters and communicating the direct purchase operational nature of the material.
When (Action): When the spare part registration is formalized in the system.

Given (Context): Given the taxonomic classification of a spare part is underway according to its technical family.
Then (Result): Then the system only presents technically valid sub-categories based on the selected superior level, ensuring accurate and standardized classification.
When (Action): When the user opens the material category selector.

Given (Context): Given the Inspector is viewing the general plant map (Level 1).
Then (Result): Then the system overlays icons over the affected equipment units, using redundant coding (Color + Shape): Hot Work: Red Square. Working at Heights: Blue Triangle. Confined Space: Yellow Circle.
When (Action): When they activate the 'Work Permits' layer.

Given (Context): Given a 'Hot Work' icon is shown over pump P-202.
Then (Result): Then a compact card is displayed (without obscuring context) with: Contractor, Start/End Time, and HSEQ Responsible.
When (Action): When the Inspector clicks on the icon.

Given (Context): Given there is an active Work Permit associated with Tag 'V-101'.
Then (Result): Then the system generates a 'Compromised Safety Integrity' alert in the notification panel and displays the permit in a lateral 'Visualization Failures' list so it does not go unnoticed.
When (Action): When the system attempts to render the icon in the 2D/3D Digital Twin and detects that the object 'V-101' does not exist in the current geometry or layout (Broken Link).

Given (Context): Given the Supervisor is viewing the General Map (Level 1).
Then (Result): Then the system smoothly transitions from the general area layout to displaying individual equipment unit icons and finally to the equipment's technical detail (Level 3).
When (Action): When they zoom into the 'Boilers' area.

Given (Context): Given the Supervisor has reached the maximum allowed detail level.
Then (Result): Then the view locks smoothly via a damping animation to prevent loss of visual context.
When (Action): When they attempt to zoom in further.

Given (Context): Given the Supervisor is inspecting a specific equipment unit in maximum detail.
Then (Result): Then the camera zooms out until the entire process unit is shown, restoring peripheral vision of alarms and neighboring equipment statuses.
When (Action): When they select 'General View' or perform a fast zoom out.

Given (Context): Given the Technician has selected a pump in the viewer and the exploded model is available.
Then (Result): Then the model parts separate visually with a fluid animation, allowing internal components like the shaft and bearings to be seen.
When (Action): When they select the 'View Exploded' option.

Given (Context): Given the equipment unit is in 'Exploded View' mode.
Then (Result): Then the system highlights the component and displays a card with its name, part code, and inventory availability at the time of query.
When (Action): When the Technician selects a specific bearing.

Given (Context): Given the Technician has selected a Work Order on their device.
Then (Result): Then the Digital Twin highlights the energy route and the lockout points on the corresponding 2D/3D view.
User Story: Isolation Route (LOTO) and Active Lock Visualization (https://app.notion.com/p/Isolation-Route-LOTO-and-Active-Lock-Visualization-39287c56a82880378ba0c0670575efe9?pvs=21)
When (Action): When they activate the 'View LOTO Route' function.

Given (Context): Given the LOTO connection lines are displayed.
Then (Result): Then the system displays the panel tag (Tag) that matches the physical reality.
User Story: Isolation Route (LOTO) and Active Lock Visualization (https://app.notion.com/p/Isolation-Route-LOTO-and-Active-Lock-Visualization-39287c56a82880378ba0c0670575efe9?pvs=21)
When (Action): When the Technician selects the suggested isolation point (e.g., Breaker).

Scenario: Start Lock due to Detected Energy
Given (Context): Given the IoT simulator reports active energy levels above the safety threshold.
Then (Result): Then the system blocks the action in the interface and displays a clear hazard alert.
User Story: Isolation Route (LOTO) and Active Lock Visualization (https://app.notion.com/p/Isolation-Route-LOTO-and-Active-Lock-Visualization-39287c56a82880378ba0c0670575efe9?pvs=21)
When (Action): When the technician attempts to press 'Start Work'.

Given (Context): Given the IoT simulator confirms there is no active energy at the isolation points.
Then (Result): Then the system allows changing the WO status to 'In Execution'.
User Story: Isolation Route (LOTO) and Active Lock Visualization (https://app.notion.com/p/Isolation-Route-LOTO-and-Active-Lock-Visualization-39287c56a82880378ba0c0670575efe9?pvs=21)
When (Action): When the technician confirms the physical lockout on the checklist.

Given (Context): Given the system cannot establish communication with the zone's IoT telemetry source.
Then (Result): Then the system preventively blocks the operation, informing that Zero Energy cannot be guaranteed due to lack of real-time data.
User Story: Isolation Route (LOTO) and Active Lock Visualization (https://app.notion.com/p/Isolation-Route-LOTO-and-Active-Lock-Visualization-39287c56a82880378ba0c0670575efe9?pvs=21)
When (Action): When the technician attempts to start work or confirm isolation.

Given (Context): Given the Engineer is on the page of equipment unit 'Pump P-101' which has no defined components.
Then (Result): Then 'Electric Motor' must appear as a nested sub-item under 'Pump P-101' in the equipment tree.
When (Action): When they click 'Add Component', name it 'Electric Motor', and assign code 'ME-01'.

Scenario: Associate a 3D model to a component
Given (Context): Given the Engineer is editing the properties of the 'Electric Motor' component.
Then (Result): Then the system must associate that 3D file with the component and display a thumbnail preview.
When (Action): When they use the 'Upload 3D Model' option and attach a motor.step file.

Given (Context): Given the Technician is viewing the equipment unit 'Pump P-101' in the mobile app.
Then (Result): Then the app must display the information and the 3D model specific to the 'Electric Motor', not the entire pump.
When (Action): When they click the exploded view and select the 'Electric Motor'.

Given (Context): Given the Engineer is adding a component.
Then (Result): Then the system prevents the creation and displays a uniqueness error message.
When (Action): When they enter a code that already belongs to another component in the same equipment unit hierarchy.

Given (Context): Given a hierarchical tree with multiple defined components.
Then (Result): Then the system updates the hierarchical relationship and displays the component in its new nested position.
When (Action): When the Engineer drags a component (e.g., 'Valve') and drops it under another parent component (e.g., 'Pipe').

Given (Context): Given the Administrator is in the roles module.
Then (Result): Then the system saves the role, ensuring any assigned user cannot modify or create records.
User Story: Role and Permission Matrix Management (Industrial RBAC) (https://app.notion.com/p/Role-and-Permission-Matrix-Management-Industrial-RBAC-39287c56a82880cb8ecbdb8f543ca3ba?pvs=21)
When (Action): When they create a new role 'External Auditor' and select only 'Read' permissions for Work Orders.

Given (Context): Given a user with a 'Technician' role is authenticated.
Then (Result): Then the system rejects the access and displays a 403 Forbidden error, logging the security event.
User Story: Role and Permission Matrix Management (Industrial RBAC) (https://app.notion.com/p/Role-and-Permission-Matrix-Management-Industrial-RBAC-39287c56a82880cb8ecbdb8f543ca3ba?pvs=21)
When (Action): When they attempt to access the 'Settings' module via URL manipulation.

Given (Context): Given an active user is logged in.
Then (Result): Then the user is automatically logged out or blocked upon their next system interaction.
User Story: Role and Permission Matrix Management (Industrial RBAC) (https://app.notion.com/p/Role-and-Permission-Matrix-Management-Industrial-RBAC-39287c56a82880cb8ecbdb8f543ca3ba?pvs=21)
When (Action): When the Administrator immediately revokes their permissions from the dashboard.

Given (Context): Given an employee contract has ended.
Then (Result): Then the user's login credentials are disabled, but their associated historical records and audits remain intact.
User Story: User Management and Secure Life Cycle (https://app.notion.com/p/User-Management-and-Secure-Life-Cycle-39287c56a828805593eaccd88c063e0f?pvs=21)
When (Action): When the Administrator marks the user profile as 'Inactive'.

Given (Context): Given a user has valid credentials.
Then (Result): Then the system authenticates the session and redirects them to their role-specific dashboard.
User Story: User Management and Secure Life Cycle (https://app.notion.com/p/User-Management-and-Secure-Life-Cycle-39287c56a828805593eaccd88c063e0f?pvs=21)
When (Action): When they input their username and password in the portal.

Given (Context): Given a user enters incorrect passwords multiple times.
Then (Result): Then the system locks the account temporarily and sends an alert to the Administrator.
User Story: User Management and Secure Life Cycle (https://app.notion.com/p/User-Management-and-Secure-Life-Cycle-39287c56a828805593eaccd88c063e0f?pvs=21)
When (Action): When they reach the maximum threshold of 5 failed attempts.

Given (Context): Given the ERP sync process is scheduled nightly.
Then (Result): Then the system immediately triggers the data exchange protocol with the ERP endpoint.
When (Action): When the Administrator clicks 'Force Synchronization Now'.

Given (Context): Given an ERP synchronization attempt fails due to timeout.
Then (Result): Then it logs the error, alerts the Administrator, and queues the payload for automatic retry on the next cycle.
When (Action): When the system detects the failure.

Given (Context): Given a global announcement is active on the user's dashboard.
Then (Result): Then the system removes the banner for that specific user while retaining it for others who haven't dismissed it.
When (Action): When the user clicks the 'Acknowledge/Dismiss' button.

Given (Context): Given a global announcement has a defined expiration date.
Then (Result): Then the system automatically hides the announcement from all user dashboards.
When (Action): When the system clock surpasses the expiration date.

Scenario: KPI Dashboard filtering by date range
Given (Context): Given the Plant Manager is viewing the Executive Dashboard.
Then (Result): Then the MTBF and MTTR metrics automatically recalculate to reflect only that specific period.
When (Action): When they adjust the date range filter to the 'Last Quarter'.

Scenario: KPI Dashboard filtering by Technical Class
Given (Context): Given the Executive Dashboard is loaded.
Then (Result): Then the displayed charts and metrics isolate the reliability data exclusively for those equipment units.
When (Action): When the user filters by the 'Centrifugal Pumps' technical class.

Given (Context): Given the Plant Manager configures a monthly KPI report.
Then (Result): Then the system automatically generates the PDF and sends it via email at the scheduled date and time.
When (Action): When they set the delivery email and schedule it for the first day of the month.

Scenario: Failed report export due to missing data
Given (Context): Given the Manager attempts to download a report for a specific month.
Then (Result): Then it displays an error message stating there is no data available to generate the report.
When (Action): When the system detects insufficient records to calculate the indicators.

Given (Context): Given the Manager is viewing the KPI Dashboard.
Then (Result): Then the system generates a compatible format file (e.g., CSV) for import into office tools.
When (Action): When they select the 'Export Structured Dataset' option.

Given (Context): Given the Manager uses an external BI tool.
Then (Result): Then the external tool imports the historical KPI data table and enables automatic updates.
When (Action): When they configure the connector with the system's programmatic API and credentials.

Given (Context): Given an equipment unit has monthly preventive maintenance and zero registered failures in the last 12 months.
Then (Result): Then the system displays a suggestion card: 'Equipment Unit [ID] shows high reliability. Suggested to decrease frequency to Bimonthly'.
When (Action): When the Supervisor accesses the PMO Optimization module.

Given (Context): Given the system displays a frequency change suggestion.
Then (Result): Then the associated Preventive Maintenance Plan is automatically updated with the new frequency, recording the approving user.
When (Action): When the Supervisor clicks 'Apply Change'.

Given (Context): Given the Administrator is in the 'General Settings' screen.
Then (Result): Then the logo in the top navigation bar immediately updates to reflect the new image.
When (Action): When they upload an image file (PNG/JPG) into the 'Corporate Logo' field and save.

Given (Context): Given the Administrator is in regional settings and the current time is UTC.
Then (Result): Then all dates and times shown on Work Orders automatically adjust to the newly selected zone.
When (Action): When they select 'UTC-5 (Colombia)' from the dropdown list.

Given (Context): Given a Planner changes a Work Order's 'Priority' from 'High' to 'Low'.
Then (Result): Then the system automatically logs an audit entry detailing: Who, When, Entity, and the specific field change from 'High' to 'Low'.
When (Action): When they save the changes.

Given (Context): Given the Auditor is investigating the history of equipment unit 'Pump P-101'.
Then (Result): Then they view a complete timeline of all status changes, maintenance, and attribute modifications since its creation.
When (Action): When they filter the audit log by the specific entity ID.

Given (Context): Given a user attempts to delete a 'Spare Part' record from the master inventory.
Then (Result): Then the system marks the record as inactive (Soft-Delete) and creates a 'DELETE_ATTEMPT' audit entry with the provided justification.
When (Action): When they confirm the action.

Given (Context): Given the Technician selects an equipment unit whose exploded model is not loaded in the repository.
Then (Result): Then the system displays a clear notice that the model is unavailable without blocking access to the rest of the details panel.
When (Action): When they attempt to activate the 'View Exploded' option.

Given (Context): Given the Planner is authenticated and the equipment unit has a configured usage sensor.
Then (Result): Then the system saves the plan and displays the current counter value alongside the target activation value.
User Story: Usage or Telemetry-Based Preventive Maintenance Scheduling (https://app.notion.com/p/Usage-or-Telemetry-Based-Preventive-Maintenance-Scheduling-39287c56a8288004b31df9fc4c104021?pvs=21)
When (Action): When they define a preventive plan setting an activation threshold (e.g., every 1000 operating hours).

Given (Context): Given an active preventive plan is configured to trigger at 5000 operating hours.
Then (Result): Then the system automatically generates the preventive Work Order and updates the target for the next intervention.
User Story: Usage or Telemetry-Based Preventive Maintenance Scheduling (https://app.notion.com/p/Usage-or-Telemetry-Based-Preventive-Maintenance-Scheduling-39287c56a8288004b31df9fc4c104021?pvs=21)
When (Action): When the Plant SCADA/IoT transmits a reading that meets or exceeds the threshold.

Given (Context): Given the system receives real-time telemetry readings.
Then (Result): Then the system rejects the reading, generates a data inconsistency alert, and maintains the counter at its last valid value.
User Story: Usage or Telemetry-Based Preventive Maintenance Scheduling (https://app.notion.com/p/Usage-or-Telemetry-Based-Preventive-Maintenance-Scheduling-39287c56a8288004b31df9fc4c104021?pvs=21)
When (Action): When a usage reading lower than the historical accumulated value is received (counter decrement).

Given (Context): Given a Functional Location has an assigned physical equipment unit (A) and an identical replacement unit (B) is available in the warehouse.
Then (Result): Then the system unlinks unit (A) setting its status to 'In Repair', links unit (B) to the location setting it to 'Operational', and logs the structural audit transaction.
When (Action): When the user executes the swap action, associating it to a Work Order.

Scenario: Swap blocked due to non-operational replacement
Given (Context): Given the user selects a replacement equipment unit from inventory.
Then (Result): Then the system blocks the swap process, issues an incompatibility alert, and does not alter the location's configuration.
When (Action): When said unit is in 'Damaged' or 'Decommissioned' status, or already assigned elsewhere.

Given (Context): Given a successful equipment unit swap was completed.
Then (Result): Then the system presents a timeline of all physical equipment units installed at that operational position, detailing installation and removal dates.
When (Action): When the technical history of the Functional Location is queried.

Given (Context): Given the user accesses the Digital Twin module.
Then (Result): Then the system renders the corresponding 2D vector layout using a neutral color palette.
When (Action): When they select a Functional Location (e.g., 'Pumping Station').

Given (Context): Given the interactive layout is loaded.
Then (Result): Then the system displays a contextual panel with the summarized technical record, lifecycle status, and active Work Orders.
When (Action): When the user interacts with the graphical representation of a specific equipment unit.

Given (Context): Given the user has the inspection panel open for an equipment unit.
Then (Result): Then the panel updates the telemetry values (e.g., pressure, temperature) in real-time without reloading the interface.
When (Action): When the Plant SCADA publishes new readings from physical sensors.

Given (Context): Given the user attempts to locate an equipment unit from the side directory.
Then (Result): Then the system displays the tabular information but disables the 'Locate on Map' function, indicating the visual mapping is pending.
When (Action): When the equipment unit has no graphical representation linked on the current layout.
